title: BRUCK SYNDROME 2
alt_titles: OSTEOGENESIS IMPERFECTA WITH CONGENITAL JOINT CONTRACTURES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene (601865) on chromosome 3q24.

checks.claim: Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Two probands were found with a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2, indicating that specific inactivation of the longer protein isoform encoded by this gene is sufficient to cause BS.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports homozygous PLOD2 mutations in Bruck syndrome (BS) and compound heterozygous mutations in a brother with mild BS.

checks.claim: The PLOD2 gene is located on chromosome 3q24.
checks.evidence_quote: two mutations in the lysyl hydroxylase 2 gene (PLOD2, 3q23-q24) have been identified in BS
checks.explanation: The paper places PLOD2 at 3q23-q24, which includes 3q24. The draft's band is standard gene-location nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome is characterized by osteoporosis, joint contractures, fragile bones, and short stature (Bank et al., 1999). Bruck syndrome-2 is the form caused by mutation in the PLOD2 gene, which encodes a telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase. The disorder is marked by a deficiency of pyridinoline cross-links in bone collagen (van der Slot et al., 2003; Ha-Vinh et al., 2004).

paragraphs.text: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) reported a boy with Bruck syndrome who was born with congenital contractures with pterygia. He also had severe osteopenia resembling osteogenesis imperfecta and multiple fractures. The authors suggested that the combination of pterygia and bone fragility implied a role for telopeptide lysyl hydroxylation in prenatal joint formation and morphogenesis.

paragraphs.text: Bank et al. (1999) studied patients with Bruck syndrome. In bone, lysine residues within the telopeptides of type I collagen were underhydroxylated, which led to aberrant crosslinking, whereas lysine residues in the triple helix were modified normally. In contrast, telopeptide hydroxylation was unaltered in cartilage and ligament, as shown by normal crosslinking patterns.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of Bruck syndrome-2 is autosomal recessive. Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) found a homozygous PLOD2 mutation in an affected boy. Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) found homozygous or compound heterozygous PLOD2 mutations in patients from consanguineous families and in a pair of brothers.

paragraphs.text: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) noted that Bruck syndrome is genetically heterogeneous. One locus had been mapped to 17p12 (BS type 1), whereas mutations in PLOD2 on 3q23-q24 cause BS type 2. They noted that it was still uncertain what proportion of cases belongs to each type, and that phenotypic correlations were lacking.

paragraphs.text: In a boy with Bruck syndrome-2, Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) identified a novel homozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene that resulted in an arg598-to-his (R598H) substitution. At birth the boy had congenital contractures with pterygia, severe osteopenia, and multiple fractures. The mutation lay next to 2 previously reported mutations, gly601-to-val and thr608-to-ile, and the authors suggested that this region is a functionally important hotspot in PLOD2. The patient's urine contained high amounts of hydroxyproline but low amounts of collagen crosslink degradation products.
